messages:
kai: Heads-up — started seeing a correlated uptick in Xid 13 and 31 on eu-west1 A10 pool over the last 3 deploy windows. Rate ~0.6%% of sessions, mostly small chat batches (<8 tokens).
leah: interesting. any infra changes rolled out to that pool recently? autoscaler, batcher, or kernel updates?
kai: rolled a small change to the continuous-batcher config two nights ago to prefer smaller batch-timeouts for low-latency chat tenants. no kernel changes.
devon: can you paste the sample logs? Xid payloads, op types, model names
kai: copied a clipped example from node-124:
```
[2026-02-10T03:12:45Z] GPU0 Xid 13: TEX_FATAL (peer memory) op=decode model=redwood-lite-4-quant
request_id=aa8f... tenant=chatlite batch_size=2 seq=48
KV_usage: 32MB, BatcherLatencyMs: 7
```
aj: Xid 13 here usually points to peer-memory/TEX faults. On A10 we've seen this surface when small-batch churn + frequent context swaps (kv evicts) happen. Could be KV cache thrash.
leah: do we have correlation with large numbers of persistent small sessions from specific tenants? maybe tenant mix changed after PLG campaign
kai: yes, top offending tenants are two PLG accounts with lots of tiny requests. They’ve increased % of traffic from ~5%% to 22%% in eu-west1 since Friday.
devon: what's the card health? ECC counters, thermal, pcie errors
kai: ECC counters modestly higher on affected GPUs but not at threshold. Temp steady ~68C. Not seeing pcie resets, just Xid13/31 bursts on the card.
sre-bot: [monitor] Alert: eu-west1-a10 pool Xid13 spike 420->650 events last 3h, top nodes: node-122,node-124,node-126
aj: hypothesis: bursty tiny batches -> frequent KV desync + increased shared memory pressure -> kernel triggers TEX fault path. Another vector: the continuous-batcher change reduced microbatch coalescing so we see smaller worklets hitting decoder kernels more often.
leah: what mitigation do we want to try? rollback batcher change? soft-drain noisy nodes? lower tenant priority?
devon: quick plan:
- Step 1: revert batcher timeout to previous value in eu-west1 edge (rollback flag ready)
- Step 2: temporarily increase KV cache retention for small sessions for 2 hours (soft throttling eviction)
- Step 3: set transient eviction threshold: if a GPU has >150 Xid events/10m, mark for soft-drain and reprovision
- Step 4: collect detailed per-op telemetry and request staging to see op mix
Kai: +1. I'll kick off step 1 now. If we don't see improvement in 20m, enable step 2.
aj: for step 3, let's be careful with auto-eviction — we don't want churn. Recommend soft-drain (no new allocations, let existing finish) and automated ticket creation for hardware follow-up if Xid persists after reprovision.
leah: agree. also add a temporary routing rule to steer the two noisy tenants to a separate quota-limited pool to protect general latency.
devon: telemetry items to collect (I'll enable): per-gpu kv_usage_histogram, optype distribution, batch_size histogram, pcie_errors, ecc_counts, and kernel_invocation_rate. store for 6h.
sre-bot: [action] rollback-config applied: continuous-batcher.timeout -> 8ms (prev 5ms) in eu-west1. Monitoring in progress.
kai: rollback in. initial Xid rate dropped ~30%% in 10m. still above baseline.
aj: good signal. next enable KV retention tweak and tenant routing. Can someone run repro on node-124 with the smallest synthetic chat job to reproduce?
leah: I'll schedule a controlled repro at 10:40 UTC and tag oncall.
kai: flagged oncall and running repro now. copying raw logs to /tmp/xid-repro-4300001111.log
devon: if repro produces a stable Xid, recommend draining and replacing the card after repro proves it’s reproducible post rollback. also open hardware ticket if ECC increments keep rising.
leah: agreed. low-risk timeline:
- 10m monitor post-KV tweak
- if still >50%% of baseline, run repro
- if repro reproduces, soft-drain node, reprovision, and escalate
kai: thanks all. will update here after the repro run completes. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: [monitor] eu-west1 Xid13 rate: 310 events in last 10m (down from 650). keeping watch.
kai: repro finished — we reproduced a single Xid 13 on node-124 under synthetic small-batch churn. Sending logs to #incidents and opening a ticket.
leah: nice work. later we should add a heuristic to the allocator to detect high small-batch churn tenants and route them to a separate soft-isolated pool to reduce cross-tenant kernel thrash.
aj: agreed. let's capture the alloc heuristics as RFC after 24h data. For now mitigation seems effective.
kai: closing loop: enabled tenant routing + soft-drain thresholds. Will follow up with postmortem if hardware replacement needed.
